comparator.name: Archaeology
comparator.sourceNotes: Leiden's adopted 2026-2027 Archaeology regulations state that the programme no longer has specialisations for new entrants; World Archaeology and Heritage and Society remain applicable only to students who started in or before 2025-2026. The same regulations establish a 180-EC degree with 150 EC of compulsory components and up to 30 EC of optional study. The live study product fully identifies the new generic 60-EC first year, but its later-year 40-EC World Archaeology and Heritage and Society groups are explicitly the outgoing specialisation structure. Combining the new generic first year with either legacy specialisation would invent an unconfirmed 2026-entrant pathway. The twelve current 5-EC first-year components below are supported. Zero-credit World Archaeology submodules and the zero-credit Active Bystander item are omitted; superseded duplicate module records also present in the product are not counted.

components.name: World Archaeology 1: Human Origins and Prehistory of the Near East
World Archaeology 2: Holocene European Prehistory and the Classical World
World Archaeology 3: Historical Archaeology and America's across 1492
Introduction to Heritage Studies: Museum Context
Introduction to Heritage Studies: Sites in Context

exception.reason: Current official sources establish the complete 60-EC generic first year for students entering Archaeology in 2026-2027, but do not publish a complete second- and third-year pathway for that new non-specialised cohort. The adopted regulations expressly limit the displayed World Archaeology and Heritage and Society specialisations to students who started in or before 2025-2026, while the live study product still uses those legacy 40-EC second-year blocks. A coherent current-entrant 180-EC comparator cannot therefore be certified without importing an outgoing route that the regulations say does not apply.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported first year covers human origins and Near Eastern prehistory; European prehistory and Classical archaeology; historical archaeology and the Americas; natural and cultural landscapes; material studies; field techniques and a field school; museum and site heritage; archaeological data analysis; and disciplinary history and future practice. The current OER confirms 150 EC of compulsory study and up to 30 EC of optional study for the 180-EC programme, but the prospectus does not identify the remaining 120 EC for the new generic cohort separately from legacy specialisation groups. Because the external-programme gate fails, no terminal UCR match assessment or UCR alternative is published. Revisit the target when Leiden publishes the later-year requirements for the post-specialisation curriculum.
